title: Harness calibration suites and runner healthchecks for onboarding profiles
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Model onboarding currently produces performance profiles that vary significantly between eval runs because of subtle dataset sampling differences, runner initialization non-determinism, and missing runner-level health signals. That makes automated version pinning and publish gates noisy.

Goal: Build a set of harness-side calibration and healthcheck primitives that reduce variance in profile generation and surface actionable signals for pinning decisions. Deliverables: 1) a calibration suite (deterministic seedbank, warmup scenarios, prefix/KV-cache warmups), 2) a dataset-contract verifier (schema, tokenization sanity, length distribution fingerprinting), 3) runner healthcheck hooks (GPU memory pressure, kernel fallbacks, quantization compatibility warnings), and 4) a small publish checklist & gating metadata fields that get attached to the generated profile artifact.

Acceptance criteria:
- Generated profiles include stable median latency, p95, throughput, and kv-cache hit rate across 3 consecutive runs (<5% variance for median latency).
- Dataset-contract verifier flags mismatched tokenizers or truncation behavior and blocks publish when critical.
- Runner healthcheck emits machine-readable warnings for fallback behaviors (e.g., kernel fallback, OOM-resize).
- Profile artifact contains a "calibration_report" field (metadata stringified) and a link to the harness run log.

Out of scope for this ticket: UI work in Console for profile display, SLA/alerting integration, and enterprise private deployment agent changes (these will follow).

implementation_notes:
Implementation approach: 1) Seedbank: expose a harness-level deterministic RNG seed parameter and persist seed per run in metadata. 2) Warmup scenarios: run 50 synthetic short-prefix inference calls per model variant to populate KV cache and primed kernels. 3) Dataset verifier: compute tokenizer fingerprint, token-length distribution quantiles, presence of special tokens, and sample a 0.1% corpus leak check against blocklisted patterns. 4) Runner healthcheck: instrument runtime to emit concise JSON health events (kernel_fallbacks, oom_resizes, cuda_driver_warnings) and surface these in calibration_report. 5) Publishing: attach calibration_report and a stable-run signature to the profile artifact and only allow auto-publish when variance < threshold and no critical healthchecks.

Trade-offs discussed: full determinism requires more synthetic warmup runs which increase cost; we opted for a small fixed warmup (50 requests) configurable per project. Tokenizer fingerprinting is language-agnostic but can miss subtle normalization differences; added human review override for rare languages.
testing_plan: 1) Integration: run the harness calibration pipeline across three model variants (llama-2-70b, mixtral-7b, internally-tuned-8k) on staging dedicated nodes and assert variance metrics. 2) Regression: include calibration_report checks in CI for new harness changes. 3) Fuzz: run dataset-contract verifier against intentionally malformed corpora to verify fail-fast behavior. 4) Canary: enable auto-publish gating for internal teams only for 2 weeks before broad rollout.
rollout_notes: Step 1: Merge PRs behind a feature flag. Step 2: Run full calibration on 10 recently onboarded models and inspect reports. Step 3: Enable auto-publish gate for model-onboarding project only. Step 4: After 2 weeks and no regressions, flip default to "opt-in" for other projects, and schedule Console UI follow-up for visualization. Monitor via dashboard: ENG-519207/summary.
open_questions: Should warmup count be adaptive based on model size (we currently plan fixed 50 but larger models may need more)?
What threshold for variance is acceptable for p95 latency when pinning versions? Suggested: <8% but PM wants <5% for customer-facing SLAs.
Do we expose calibration_report fields in the public profile API or keep them internal to Console?
